assumptions.text: The USD amount is the amount to be received in the US. The CNY converted is USD x the BOC spot selling rate on 2026-11-10 (S16).
assumptions.why: Fees are charged in CNY; a rate is needed to express them in USD.
assumptions.impact: Moves the fixed-fee USD figure by <0.3% for a +/-2% rate change.

assumptions.text: FX markup on the CNY->USD leg is 0.2098%, the half-spread between BOC's published spot selling rate (6.6851) and the midpoint of its published bid/ask (6.6711).
assumptions.why: No regulator publishes a spread; this is arithmetic on one dated official quotation.
assumptions.impact: Directly scales with amount: USD 20.98 per USD 10,000. A bank quoting 1% would cost about 5x this line.

assumptions.text: The HSBC China Advance/Premier telegraphic-transfer tariff applies (0.1%, min CNY 100, max CNY 500, plus CNY 120 cable).
assumptions.why: It is the only dated, published per-transfer fee schedule verified in this session.
assumptions.impact: Fixed CNY 220 at the low end; capped at CNY 620 above ~CNY 500,000 of principal.

assumptions.text: The receiving US bank charges USD 16 per incoming international wire (BofA Interest Checking, S15). No intermediary-bank deduction is included.
assumptions.why: Intermediary deductions are not published anywhere I could verify.
assumptions.impact: Understates the true deduction if a correspondent bank takes a fee.
assumptions.status: one bank, one account type; intermediary fees excluded

assumptions.text: No tax is included in the all-in cost columns.
assumptions.why: A conversion tax depends on acquisition rates and filing history that are private facts.
assumptions.impact: See taxes.html for the conditional section 988 layer; it is shown separately, never merged.

assumptions.text: Statutory penalty ceilings (30% of amount) are shown only for unlawful routes, as the legal maximum, never as an expected cost.
assumptions.why: The statutes set a range up to 30% (30%-100% if serious); no authority publishes an average.

tax_layer.formula: gain = USD received x (1 - conversion_rate / acquisition_rate)
tax_layer.note: Rate history is from S12; the conversion rate is the dated BOC selling rate in S16. These are illustrations of the arithmetic, not a tax computation for any person.
